Topics · Hard times

If God is merciful, why does He let us suffer?

No complete answer is known. The Quran holds to mercy, says life has weight. Nothing here silences your pain.

If you are in pain right now, you do not have to carry it alone. Please reach out to someone you trust, or to a local crisis line or emergency number. Find a helpline near you

Part 1 of 4

﴿وَإِذَا جَآءَكَ ٱلَّذِينَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِـَٔايَـٰتِنَا فَقُلْ سَلَـٰمٌ عَلَيْكُمْ ۖ كَتَبَ رَبُّكُمْ عَلَىٰ نَفْسِهِ ٱلرَّحْمَةَ ۖ أَنَّهُۥ مَنْ عَمِلَ مِنكُمْ سُوٓءًۢا بِجَهَـٰلَةٍ ثُمَّ تَابَ مِنۢ بَعْدِهِۦ وَأَصْلَحَ فَأَنَّهُۥ غَفُورٌ رَّحِيمٌ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And when those come to you who believe in Our verses, say, "Peace be upon you. Your Lord has decreed upon Himself mercy: that any of you who does wrong out of ignorance and then repents after that and corrects himself - indeed, He is Forgiving and Merciful."

Quran · Al-An'am 6:54

Translation

Tell them, ‘“As I live,” says the Lord Yahweh, “I have no pleasure in the death of the wicked, but that the wicked turn from his way and live. Turn, turn from your evil ways! For why will you die, house of Israel?”’

Original · Hebrew

אֱמֹ֨ר אֲלֵיהֶ֜ם חַי־אָ֣נִי ׀ נְאֻ֣ם ׀ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֗ה אִם־אֶחְפֹּץ֙ בְּמ֣וֹת הָרָשָׁ֔ע כִּ֣י אִם־בְּשׁ֥וּב רָשָׁ֛ע מִדַּרְכּ֖וֹ וְחָיָ֑ה שׁ֣וּבוּ שׁ֜וּבוּ מִדַּרְכֵיכֶ֧ם הָרָעִ֛ים וְלָ֥מָּה תָמ֖וּתוּ בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

Ezekiel · 33:11

World English Bible

You are not accusing anyone unfairly. Your question is built from the book's own words. It does not describe God as distant or indifferent. It says mercy is something He has written upon Himself, the strongest thing it could say, and that raises what a person may hope for. If a stranger ignored your pain, you would be hurt. If the One called merciful seems silent, you are shaken. The ache in this question comes from taking the word seriously.

A question for you

Where does this question come from for you today?

If you sayFrom something that hurts.
ThenThen nothing here needs to be solved today. Read only what helps, and leave the rest.
If you sayFrom someone I love.
ThenThen you are asking on their behalf, which is a form of love. What follows tries to be worthy of them.
If you sayFrom my reason. It does not add up.
ThenThat is a fair place to begin. The next part says what the Quran claims about the world, and where that claim stops.
If you sayFrom anger at easy answers.
ThenThat anger has its reasons. You will find no easy answer here.

Quran · Al-Mulk 67:2

Translation

I know also, my God, that you try the heart and have pleasure in uprightness. As for me, in the uprightness of my heart I have willingly offered all these things. Now I have seen with joy your people, who are present here, offer willingly to you.

Original · Hebrew

וְיָדַ֣עְתִּי אֱלֹהַ֔י כִּ֤י אַתָּה֙ בֹּחֵ֣ן לֵבָ֔ב וּמֵישָׁרִ֖ים תִּרְצֶ֑ה אֲנִ֗י בְּיֹ֤שֶׁר לְבָבִי֙ הִתְנַדַּ֣בְתִּי כָל־אֵ֔לֶּה וְעַתָּ֗ה עַמְּךָ֙ הַנִּמְצְאוּ־פֹ֔ה רָאִ֥יתִי בְשִׂמְחָ֖ה לְהִֽתְנַדֶּב־לָֽךְ׃

1 Chronicles · 29:17

World English Bible

Here is what the book does not promise: a life without pain. It says the human being was made into strain, and that life and death exist for something, which it names as the chance to act well. So mercy, in this account, cannot simply mean that nothing hurts. It would have to mean something else: that pain is not the last word, that no good is lost, that no one is unseen. Whether that is enough is a fair question, and it stays open.

A question for you

Which comes closest to what you want mercy to mean?

If you sayThat the pain would stop.
ThenThat is the plainest and truest human wish. Nothing here calls it weak.
If you sayThat I would not be alone in it.
ThenThen the question becomes who is near, and the Quran says a great deal about that.
If you sayThat it would mean something in the end.
ThenThen what matters to you is whether anything is lost. Another Step takes that up.

כִּ֣י לֹ֤א מַחְשְׁבוֹתַי֙ מַחְשְׁב֣וֹתֵיכֶ֔ם וְלֹ֥א דַרְכֵיכֶ֖ם דְּרָכָ֑י נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָֽה׃ כִּֽי־גָבְה֥וּ שָׁמַ֖יִם מֵאָ֑רֶץ כֵּ֣ן גָּבְה֤וּ דְרָכַי֙ מִדַּרְכֵיכֶ֔ם וּמַחְשְׁבֹתַ֖י מִמַּחְשְׁבֹתֵיכֶֽם׃

Isaiah · 55:8-9

World English Bible

The book also names a limit: God's knowledge is whole, and ours is partial. This sentence, first said about going to battle, is easy to misuse. Said to a person in pain, it can sound like an order to stop asking. Read closely, it does something smaller. It says 'perhaps', twice. It does not call your loss good. It says human sight is limited, and that same limit means no one else can tell you what your pain means. No complete answer is known, here or anywhere.

A question for you

When someone says 'there must be a reason', what happens in you?

If you sayIt settles me.
ThenThen keep it. It is yours, and no one here will take it from you.
If you sayIt makes me angry.
ThenYou may be hearing someone claim a knowledge they do not have. Your anger may be guarding something true.
If you sayI want to believe it and cannot.
ThenMany people stand exactly there. Wanting to and being unable is no failing.

Part 4 of 4

﴿ٱلَّذِىٓ أَحْسَنَ كُلَّ شَىْءٍ خَلَقَهُۥ ۖ وَبَدَأَ خَلْقَ ٱلْإِنسَـٰنِ مِن طِينٍ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Who perfected everything which He created and began the creation of man from clay.

Quran · As-Sajdah 32:7

Translation

All the works of the Lord are exceedingly good, and every command will be done in its time.

Original · Ancient Greek

Τὰ ἔργα Κυρίου πάντα ὅτι καλὰ σφόδρα, καὶ πᾶν πρόσταγμα ἐν καιρῷ αὐτοῦ ἔσται.

Sirach · 39:16

World English Bible

This verse says He made everything well. Two Muslim scholars tried to hold that beside pain; these are thoughts, not rulings. Ibn Qayyim al-Jawziyya separated God's act, which he held to be wholly good, from what comes about through it, some of which hurts. He reasoned that forgiveness and mercy have no place in a world without need. Said Nursi separated making from doing: to set a hard thing within a larger whole is one matter, and to choose harm is another. Neither claims to explain your pain.

A question for you

Which thought, if either, gives you something to hold?

If you sayIbn Qayyim's: some good is born of need.
ThenMany have found rest in it. Its limit is that it speaks of the good that may come, and does not make the harm any smaller.
If you sayNursi's: choosing harm differs from making the world.
ThenThen the next thing to weigh is human freedom and its cost.
If you sayNeither, and that is my answer.
ThenThat is an honest answer. They are thoughts, not conditions, and you lose nothing by setting them down.
